title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a sketch of what is now called the Hodge–Tate decomposition, plus its compatibility with cycle classes. It sits on scrap paper: the neighbouring pages are a Bourbaki typescript (n° 380) on holomorphic functional calculus and are unrelated. The setting is reconstructed from the dossier (letter to Tate, May 1966) and Tate's 1966 Driebergen paper on p-divisible groups. K is a p-adic field. C is the completion of an algebraic closure of K. π = Gal(K̄/K), written as π_1(Spec K) in Grothendieck's style. χ is the cyclotomic character. X is smooth and proper over K, and X_C is its base change. The symbol H^i_B(X_C, C) must denote p-adic étale cohomology with coefficients extended to C, i.e. H^i_et(X_{K̄}, Z_p) ⊗ C with semilinear Galois action. It is not complex Betti cohomology: the later lines use Z_p[i] and π-invariants. [p] denotes Tate twist by C(p).

Conjecture 1 has three parts.
- H^i is intrinsically the direct sum of the subspaces spanned by χ^p-eigenvectors, i.e. its C(-p)-isotypic parts.
- Set H^{p,q}_B(X)_K := (H^i ⊗ C(p))^π for p+q = i. By Tate's theorem C^π = K, so this is a K-vector space.
- One then gets H^i ≅ ⊕_{p+q=i} H^{p,q}_B(X)_K ⊗_K C(-p). The decomposition is intrinsic because Tate showed (C(a))^π = 0 for a ≠ 0, so there are no Galois maps between different twists.

Conjecture 2: there is a canonical isomorphism φ^{p,q}: H^{p,q}_B(X)_K ≅ H^q(X, Ω^p_X), the Hodge cohomology over K. Together, 1) and 2) are the Hodge–Tate conjecture: H^i_et ⊗ C ≅ ⊕ H^q(X, Ω^p) ⊗_K C(-p).

Below the rule comes the cycle-class part. For a codimension-i cycle Z^i, the étale class P_B(Z^i) lies in H^{2i}(X_{K̄}, Z_p(i))^π. This maps into (H^{2i} ⊗ C(i))^π = H^{i,i}_B(X)_K. The Hodge/de Rham class P_DR(Z^i) lies in H^{i,i}(X) = H^i(X, Ω^i). The desired compatibility is φ^{ii}(P_B(Z^i)) = P_DR(Z^i). The NB records that algebraic classes lie in the intersection of the (i,i) Hodge–Tate part (identified with H^{i,i}(X)) with the integral lattice H^{2i}(Z_p(i)). This is the p-adic analogue of the fact that algebraic classes are integral (p,p)-classes in Hodge theory.

Purpose: a p-adic analogue of the Hodge decomposition and of compatibility with cycle classes, alongside the crystalline (Dieudonné-crystal) programme of the Tate letter.
errors: The notation H_B ('Betti') is used for what must be p-adic étale cohomology tensored with C. This is an abuse or a placeholder, not literal Betti cohomology.
The chain ends with '⊂ H^{2i}(X_C, Z_p)'. This is sloppy: the Z_p-lattice does not contain the C-vector space. Presumably the intended statement is that the image of H^{2i}(Z_p(i)) sits inside both.
The map H^{2i}(Z_p(i))^π → H^{i,i}_B is injective only modulo torsion. This is not noted.
No hypotheses are stated (good reduction, or arbitrary smooth proper). Tate's conjecture was formulated generally; it was proven by Faltings in 1988.

ideas.what: Intrinsic decomposition of p-adic étale cohomology ⊗ C into Tate-twist isotypic pieces, with K-structure given by Galois invariants of twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1966/67, p-divisible groups); proved by Faltings 1988 (earlier partial results by Fontaine–Messing, Bloch–Kato)
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in the 1966 letter to Tate on crystals; not in EGA/SGA as far as known

ideas.what: Canonical identification of the Galois-invariant twisted pieces with Hodge cohomology H^q(X, Ω^p)
Compatibility of the étale cycle class (in the (i,i) Hodge–Tate part) with the Hodge/de Rham cycle class under φ^{ii}
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of p-adic comparison isomorphisms with cycle classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine's formulation of the de Rham/Hodge–Tate comparison; proofs by Faltings, Tsuji, Nizioł and others

ideas.what: Algebraic classes lie in the intersection of the (i,i)-Hodge–Tate piece with the integral Z_p(i) lattice
ideas.modern_name: p-adic analogue of 'algebraic classes are integral Hodge classes'
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / implicit in Tate and Fontaine

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently writes down the Hodge–Tate conjecture in the 1966 Tate-letter / crystals dossier, in intrinsic form (isotypic parts plus Galois-invariant K-structure). The history usually attributes the conjecture solely to Tate.
missed.quote: H^i_B(X_C, C) ≃ ∐_{p+q=i} H^{p,q}_B(X)_K ⊗_K C[-p] ... φ^{p,q}: H^{p,q}_B(X)_K ≃ H^q(X, Ω^p_X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents Grothendieck's participation in the birth of p-adic Hodge theory alongside Tate. It is relevant to the history of the 'mysterious functor' and of crystalline comparison.

missed.claim: The page adds the requirement that the comparison send étale cycle classes to Hodge cycle classes. This anticipates the cycle-class compatibility later built into Fontaine's comparison conjectures.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical: it shows that the motivic and cycle-theoretic motivation was present from the start.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early (c. 1966) handwritten formulation by Grothendieck of the Hodge–Tate decomposition, including compatibility with cycle classes. The mathematics is now established (Faltings and others), and the conjecture is credited to Tate in the same period, so it is mainly of historical interest rather than containing unexploited mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'vecteurs π^p-propres' should almost certainly read 'vecteurs χ^p-propres' (cyclotomic character to the p-th power); the superscript π in '[p]^π' denotes invariants under π = Galois group.
'de façon intrinsèque, i.e. [?]' is likely 'de façon intrinsèque, posant, pour p+q=i'.
'H^{2i}_{\mathbb Z}(X_C, Z_p[i])' has a crossed-out or illegible subscript (probably 'ét'), not ℤ.
The second-line 'H^{2i}(X_C, Z_p)' has an illegible small subscript (likely 'ét').
The crossed-out text above P_DR is 'P_B(Z^i)', replaced by P_DR(Z^i) ∈ H^{i,i}(X).
In the NB, 'H^{i,i}_B(X_C)' appears as 'H^{i,i}_B(X_C, C)' with an underbrace 'identifié à H^{i,i}(X)'.
